description: Per birth country, count the player_college records matched to a player. Shares, the above-average filter and the summary are all built on those record counts.

c.request: Using the college attendance data matched to players by `player_id` (leaving out anything with no matching player), tally college attendance for each player `birth_country`, along with each country's share of the overall tally. For the countries above the average tally across all countries, give me one row: their combined tally, their average share, and on average how far above the average tally they are. No rounding. Per birth country, count the player_college records matched to a player. Shares, the above-average filter and the summary are all built on those record counts.
c.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.birth_country), s AS (SELECT birth_country, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share, (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM c) AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_tally, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_above_average FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

a.request: Match each `player_college` record to its player by `player_id`, dropping records with no matching player. Count the matched college records (one per player-college-year row) for each `birth_country`, and work out each country's share of the total of those counts. Now take only the countries whose record count is above the average record count across all countries. In one row, give the total record count of those countries, their average share, and the average amount by which their record count exceeds that overall average. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.birth_country AS country, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.birth_country), t AS (SELECT c.*, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share, (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM c) AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM t WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

b.request: Count the player_college records that match a player on `player_id` (dropping unmatched ones) for each player `birth_country`, compute each country's share of the total count of those records, keep countries whose count is above the average per-country count, and return one row with the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average of (count minus the average per-country count), all unrounded
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.birth_country), t AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.cnt) AS sum_count, AVG(c.cnt * 1.0 / t.total) AS avg_share, AVG(c.cnt - t.avg_cnt) AS avg_diff FROM c, t WHERE c.cnt > t.avg_cnt

d.request: Using the college attendance data (`player_college` records) matched to players by `player_id`, and leaving out any records with no matching player, count the `player_college` records for each player `birth_country`, and calculate each country's share of the overall total of those record counts. For the countries whose record count is above the average record count across all countries, return a single row with their combined record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their record counts exceed the average count. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.birth_country), t AS (SELECT birth_country, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share, (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM c) AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_record_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS average_excess FROM t WHERE cnt > avg_cnt
